title: Cross-region admit fabric: KV-cache-aware hedging experiments
content:
Purpose / TL;DR:
We need an admission fabric that (1) coordinates admission decisions across regions, (2) reasons about the value of requests to in-flight KV cache (prefix / KV cache hit probability), and (3) uses graded admit + hedging to avoid long tail latency when one region is overloaded. This doc captures an exploratory design and an experiment plan to test a KV-aware, GPU-utilization-driven admit controller that performs cross-region handoff and selective hedging instead of blind replication.

Why this is different from prior sketches: 
- Instead of binary accept/reject per-region we propose graded admits (fast-path/safepath/deferred) informed by a request-level KV hit estimator and recent per-GPU sequence-length distribution.
- Hedging is selective and data-aware: we only hedge when the expected marginal benefit (increase in KV hit or end-to-end latency reduction) exceeds the cost (extra GPU token and network).
- Cross-region handoff prioritizes staying with the original region when KV cache hit is likely; we avoid creating write amplification for KV-cold requests.

Design goals and constraints:
- SLOs: P50 < 40ms, P95 < 200ms for hosted-api tier; Dedicated SLOs have lower tail target and isolated capacity guarantees.
- Cost sensitivity: hedges should be budgeted per-account and per-route. Hedges are expensive on per-token basis.
- Observability: every admit decision must emit a small decision vector for later offline eval (fields listed in telemetry section).
- Safety: fall back to existing token-bucket reject if signals missing.

Key signals we use (available from runtime/ingress):
- GPU utilization (per GPU aggregated to host and region).
- Queue depth and queue wait time per ingress lane and per-model route.
- Recent KV-cache local hit rate estimator (moving window per model-shard and prefix-length bucket).
- Request-level features: prefix-length, estimated total seq_len, tenant tier, route id.
- Admission credits / token buckets per-tenant and per-route.

Admission decision model (high level):
1) Compute request value score V as a weighted function of: estimated KV hit probability p_kv(prefix, model_version), urgency weight (customer SLA), and expected token-cost (seq_len_est).
2) Map V into admit band: FAST / SLOW / DEFER / REJECT. Bands map to admission actions:
   - FAST: immediate schedule on same-region GPU with priority slot.
   - SLOW: schedule on same-region but behind preemption-protected pool (can be delayed to batch).
   - DEFER: route to cross-region cheaper capacity or queue in soft-hold for short retry; optionally attempt a single selective hedge if cross-region latency expected lower.
   - REJECT: token-bucket deny.
3) If local GPU utilization > util_hysteresis_high AND p_kv low => consider cross-region hedging if remote region util < util_hysteresis_low AND delta_lat_est < hedging_latency_budget. Hedging type: speculative-start (start remote request) OR speculative-query (probe with sub-sampled tokens to prime KV).

KV-aware heuristics (novel bits):
- p_kv estimator: small moving-model stored at ingress that maps prefix-length and model-version to hit rate. Bootstrapped from runtime stats. Avoids expensive RPCs.
- kv-score = p_kv * (1 - expected_remote_kv_penalty). If kv-score high, prefer local routing, even if local GPU util slightly higher; cache locality wins.
- sequence-length aware admission: for long seq_len requests we bias to SLOW lane to reduce head-of-line blocking. Short seq_len get FAST priority if credits allow.

Graded hedging policy (cost-aware):
- Hedge budget: per-team monthly budget (in tokens) and per-minute rate limit. Hedges consume from budget when decided.
- Hedge decision if: local_tail_risk > threshold AND estimated p_kv_local < p_kv_remote * alpha AND remote_util_gap > beta
- Hedge types: 
   * Cold-hedge: start remote execution but cancel local after remote emits first tokens (cheap for streaming).
   * KV-probe: remote-only probe that requests a small KV-only eval to warm remote caches, then route main request if probe succeeds within probe_budget_ms.

Signal handoff and consistency contract: 
- When we handoff to remote we MUST propagate request context: model_version, pinned shards, KV-reservation hint (so remote can use the same cached prefix mapping).
- If handoff happens after local partial computation (rare), we accept best-effort de-duplication; full deterministic dedupe is future work.

Telemetry fields (minimum) per-request: 
- request_id, route_id, tenant_id, prefix_len, seq_len_est, p_kv_local, p_kv_remote, local_gpu_util, remote_gpu_util, queuesz_local, admit_band, action_taken (fast/slow/defer/reject/hedge), hedge_type, hedge_cost_est, effective_latency_ms, outcome (served_local/served_remote/rejected/timeout).
- These are intentionally compact strings/numeric fields emitted as a single line to our telemetry Kafka topic.

Simulation plan (fast feedback loops):
1) Offline replay: take 48h of ingress traces, simulate different admit thresholds, and sample hedging decisions. Metrics: P95/P99 latency, total extra tokens, percent hedged, percent duplicate work, KV-hit delta.
2) Microbench: run small cluster with synthetic prefix-skew workloads (mix of KV-hot and KV-cold prefixes) to validate p_kv estimator accuracy and hedging cost modeling.
3) Canary: enable on a low-traffic region with hedging budget = 0.5% of baseline token usage, track tail latency and cost. Gradually increase if metrics meet goals.

Experiment variants to compare (A/B):
- Baseline: current token-bucket + global fallback routing. 
- Variant 1: graded admit without hedging (FAST/SLOW/DEFER), no cross-region hedges. 
- Variant 2: graded admit + blind hedging (hedge all DEFERed requests) — expected high cost. 
- Variant 3: kv-aware selective hedging (proposed) — target: lower tail with <1% tokens extra compared to baseline.

Operational runbook (short):
- If cross-region hedging causes cost spike: disable hedging by setting hedge_alpha = 1.0 and hedge_budget = 0.
- If high duplicate work observed: throttle hedging rate and enable lightweight dedupe flag for a subset of routes.
- If p_kv estimator diverges: fall back to prefix-length heuristic and schedule a stats-collection job.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to account for KV warmup energy? (starting a small probe might warm remote caches but also perturb measurements). Need an A/B experiment measuring net hit-rate vs probe overhead.
- Can we do cross-region KV sharing (probabilistic) to reduce hedging? Network cost vs hit improvements need modeling.
- Deduplication semantics for partial local progress with remote handoff (cost/complexity tradeoff).
- Better per-tenant hedging economics: allow teams to opt-in/opt-out and set budgets programmatically.

Short checklist for implementation spike:
- [ ] Implement p_kv estimator store at ingress (small memory, LRU per model-version).
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks for decision vector.
- [ ] Simulation harness to replay 48h traces with parameter sweep.
- [ ] Microbench infra: synthetic workloads for KV-hot/KV-cold mixes.
- [ ] Canary rollout plan and feature flag gate in control plane.

Notes from quick offline sim (toy numbers, 2h run with synthetic traces):
- Blind hedging reduced P99 by ~18% but increased token usage by ~27% (too expensive).
- KV-aware selective hedging reduced P99 by ~12% with token increase ~0.9% (promising).
- p_kv estimator error increased for very long prefixes (>1024 tokens) — need separate bucket or fallback to sequence-length heuristic.

References / links: 
- PLAT-4821 (admit fabric sketch)
- infra/ingress/telemetry-spec (proto fields we add)
- prior: ingress-governor-gpu-feedback-and-deferred-admit-proposal (see notes for util hysteresis values)

Concluding note:
This design tries to respect cache locality while giving us a principled, budgeted way to reduce tail latency across regions. The next step is to get a short simulation pass (2–3 days) and then a microbench to confirm the cost model before any canary.

Author notes / free-form: 
- Keep hedges conservative at first. The single most valuable improvement was selectively hedging requests that are both KV-cold and short (fast to execute) — those are cheap wins because they avoid long tail but don't add huge token costs.
- Add a small admin UI in the Console under the route to show hedging spend and allow per-route override; product likes this.
